I've been S. jonesii-ball-EFFIN this clone for years (Low Giant) and FINALLY hooked up one from www.flytrapcare.com! Check out how healthy this thing is several weeks later, Matt has some great quality plants:

Another shot of B-52. You can't tell from the pics, but these traps are absolutely enormous right now!

posts.body_html:
Venuuuus, venus-flytraps..AND JELLY! first you take the flytraps and you grow em, you grow em...LOL I'm so brainwashed by nursery rhymes, had to remixed that PB and J one!

Some updated pics of the various clones in the collection, pics taken mostly on 8/17/21:

Dionaea Scarlatine, a very interested dentate clone that turns reddish and has variegation:


Dionaea 'Orton's red side:' had this for a while, but never got a good pic until recently. Now people are starting to understand that this clone is very special:


D. muscipula Onslow Co, NC, nice color forms and diversity:


Dionaea B-52: these plants really have to be healthy to begin with, otherwise they're difficult to grow: a few growers report difficulty getting this thing to perform, and I suspect they may have started with a weak plant. I got this as a tiny plant and babied it for years until it finally got some good growth momentum. Now it performs year after year:


Dionaea 'Big Mouth.' I'm sorry, but this clone is far from having a big mouth. That said, it produces deep red traps that are quite attractive. medium vigor:


The famous Dionaea B-52, hard to tell from the pic but these traps are mostly all giant!


Dionaea G-14 rosette. In previous years, this clone has formed small rosettes and is quite attractive, but when the clone is super happy, the traps get deep red and kinda big, which detracts from its unique growth habit:


Dionaea G-17 MEGATRAPS! I wish you could tell just how big these traps are, but it's impossible to tell from the pic. Guess you just have to take my word for it:


Here we go, you can now see how big this trap is! Dionaea Colorado Giant, an excellent performer with crazy hybrid vigor and gigantic traps:


Dionaea TC clone from the 1990's: this clone can produce really big traps too! it's coloring up well this year:



A big chunk of the flytrap collection, there's more, but it's all scattered here and there:

posts.body_html:
time for some updates! I've been acquiring tons of new flytrap clones and loving every single one of them!

D. muscipula Albion #3, just recently got this one over the past winter from my homie Rob Co from the pitcher plant project and it's producing some pretty big traps already! Seems to be some unique genetics with a nice thick petiole, there's some features of it that are very subtle and hard to describe:


Dionaea Galaxy: absolutely love this one, but it grows super slow and can't catch insects, so you have to feed them. I haven't been on top of my game regarding giving them food, which is why they're still very small, but they still look good:


DCXL: I was a little disappointed with this clone: most pics showed this clone to be DCXS(Dave Connor X-tra small), but holy crapola! This thing lives up to it's name! It's super fast growing and pushes out tons of traps that are way bigger than anything else in the collection...at least at the moment:


This trap just opened, its really big when you see it in person:


Another shot of DCXL:


Dionaea La Grosse a guigui. This clone produces super long petioles and I need to take a better pic of it! I've seen other plants in google searches that make me feel insecure about the size of my guigui:



Dionaea Alien. A great grower, even outside, but it seems to stay yellowish, probably because my plant is starving! It doesn't seem to be able to catch insects and relies on artificial feeding:


Dionaea Jaws Smiley!


the reason I really like Jaws Smiley is because of the phenotypic variance this clone displays! When part of the lobe of the trap slightly bends inwards (both top and bottom of the lobes can do this), it really changes the look of the trap and gives it that smiley appearance. My clone finally did that, although only the top of the lobe bent in:


This is Jaws Smiley, but pretty indistiguishable from Alien:


Dionaea Big Mouth. This clone never did well for me until recently! they've always been slow growing with medium sized mouths, but now the mouths are starting to size up. These are just starting to look good, I think in a month or two they'll be way more stunning:


another shot of big mouth, starting to grow strong now in some new peat:


D. muscipula Onslow Co, NC. There are maybe 3-4 clones in here, one of them is giant and the other is a really nice red one! These weren't transplanted this past winter, so they're lookin really nice now:


Another shot of the Onslow Co, NC flytraps:


D. muscipula Brunswick Co, NC. These seedlings are 7 months old. first time in almost 20 years that I've sown some flytrap seeds!





More pics to come, just haven't gotten all the new ones photographed yet!

posts.body_html:
some more updates of flytrap clones, pics taken late June 2022:

La Grosse a Guigui. Now, just so I set the record straight, many others have much larger guiguis than mine, there's no competition here


Dionaea Spotty-less. The variegation with this clone isn't stable, the cut I got hasn't yet produced any spots anywhere, but here's what the clone looks like under strong light. Looks like a "watered down" yet nice red dragon type. doesn't grow fast, but isn't entirely slow either:


Dionaea Schuppenstiel I aka shop N Steal. We do not endorse stealing, only shopping:


Dionaea Monkey @ss (gluteus maximus). Gotta keep this PG-13 guys! I'm not into buttox, but I do like the way this clone looks:


Another shot of monkey glutes:


Here's G-16, been S. jonesii'in for this clone for years and finally got one! It's everything I dreamed it would be: vigorous, good looking, and great performer overall:


Another shot of Dionaea G-16:


Dionaea Giant Clam-I guess this clone is somewhat uncommon in the US? It definitely meets the hype! These were small plants last year and they've produced nice sized traps this season! Can't wait to see what this looks like when it actually gets really big!


Another shot of giant clam:

posts.body_html:
Some more flytrap obsession shots, taken early July 2022. Here's an overview of the biggest chunk of flytraps in the collection, they're sorta scattered all over the place. Most of these were repotted this past winter, so they're just starting to push out traps. In 1-2 months, these will be much more impressive:


D. muscipula Onslow Co, NC. There's about 4 different clones in this pot, and they're doing very well this year:


Another shot, why not?


Dionaea 'Grun' the traps this year are getting surprisingly big, we'll see if they get gigantic in a few weeks. There's a massive flush of new traps just starting to develop now on most of the flytraps. I got this clone from my homie Drew Martinez many years ago, and when I first got it, I thought...hmmm, G-Run? what the heck? Turns out, it's German (?) for green and is pronounced "GROON" as far as I know, feel free to correct me if this isn't right:


Neglected for nearly a decade and then recently transplanted this past winter. Looking much better this year, should have taken a pic the past few years, these plants looks absolutely horrible!


DCXL to the left, big tomato the right. DCXL is producing traps bigger than anything else in the collection right now, but I don't think they're gigantic yet. Without a doubt, this clone is a winner, had it for a little less than a year and it's already sizing up!


Another shot. From left to right(front row): DCXL, big tomato, and monkey[bad word]. Such a horrible name, even for someone who swears on a daily like myself:


A bunch of the "new" plants, not going to bother trying to name them all:


Dionaea Wolverine. Decent vigor and not too picky about environmental conditions to get good growth:


some older clones that have been in the collection for a while, just starting to push out decent traps after being transplanted. Still need a few more weeks before these look worthy, but given all the new traps that have all of the sudden just started to emerge, I think there will be a good show in the near future:

posts.body_html:
This is the BE clone, growing in blasting full sun, literally from sun up till sunset! Whenever it gets over 85F, I hide it under some Sarraecnia. Almost everywhere else, this plant would perish in full sun from overheating, but it's mostly cold here all summer long, so they love it:

Some updated pics of the flytrap collection, taken 7/11/22:

Another shot of a big chunk of the flytrap collection, there's more but this is the bulk of it:


TRD red dragon! No, it's not a TRD, its The Real Deal!


One of my favorite flytrap clones, SD Draco aka STEEVIE DOONAN Draco. Photos of it elsewhere don't do this justice! This clone has red traps even in part shade, although this one is currently growing in full sun:



SD Draco:


SD Draco:


I was checking out my guigui the other day and noticed it has some variegation going on! completely unexpected but extremely cool and super happy to see this:


La Grosse a guigui


One last shot:


Look how weird this one is! Dionaea Albion #3. This is only from one trap, it's not stable:


Coquillage: when this flowered, I pinched them off, but it took MONTHS before new growth started again! The plant looked like it was going to die but then it busted out with some new growth:


Not a lot of pictures of this clone out there, this is Dionaea 'Big tomato'

posts.body_html:
some updated pics of mostly "new" flytrap clones, taken mostly on 8/30/22:

Coquillage: earlier in the spring, this clone produced two flower spikes, and I pinched them early on. Almost 3 months later, it still had ZERO new traps and all of the older traps were turning yellow, so I thought it was jacked or in decline. Then all of the sudden, it produced a ton of new traps and here it is now:


LOWWW Giant, everybody down, LowWWWW GIant cuz we're going through town. and you'll always know your neighbor, you'll always know your pal if you've ever navigated on the eerie canal!


Monkey Buttox (just to be PG-13):


SD Draco, one of my favorites! Not big, but colorful all year round, even with less than optimal lighting:


HELP! My GUIGUI SHRUNK!!!! hehe You can see the taller, summer traps, and now the newer ones are shorter, probably so that it can gear down for the winter dormancy period.


Wolverine: a great performer! I had my doubts about this clone, but turns out it's really vigorous and showy:


Another shot of wolverine:


Schuppensteil I, even without the weird mutant petioles, this clone is pretty impressive:


Now we have ginormous prepared two ways:
1) potted:

and 2) in a community tray:


And last but not least, maroon monster looking amazing! The green petioles contrasting with the dark red traps....mama mia!

posts.body_html:
some updated pics, taken 10/13/22. SD draco steals the show:


Low Giant. got this from Matt at flytrapcare.com in June 2021, and it arrived as a large, healthy plant. Here it is about 14 months later! Very healthy starter plants yield impressive results when properly cared for! BTW, that's not a weed in the pot, it's a calopogon tuberosus seedling that showed up this year from seed:


Shuppensteil I still looking decent:


SD Kronos had a rough start, but is finally settling in.


Giant microdent:


Dionaea R638N-this thing grows like no other clone! It's very 3 dimensional, so it's hard to photograph. Probably tripled in size since I got it around 5 months ago. Selected and bred by Ron Determann(sp?) of Atlanta Botanical Gardens, and those guys have an enormous library of genetics to play with, so it's no surprise this clone is an absolute winner:




one last shot of R638N. Ron's naming system makes him look pretty smart and plant nerdy. Much respect:
